title: Spec
description: One unit of planned work: durable context, plus an optional ordered list of issues. Written by /to-spec (without issues), populated by /to-issues, executed one issue per iteration by loop.sh. Everything here is written once and read many times, so every field is chosen for what a fresh agent needs in a context window that contains nothing else.

slug.description: Kebab-case identifier for the effort. Must match the containing directory name.

summary.description: What this effort changes and why, in 1-3 sentences. INJECTED INTO EVERY LOOP ITERATION — keep it short enough that repeating it costs nothing.

context.description: Long-form background: research, provenance, rejected alternatives, links. Prefer writing this to a sibling <spec-dir>/context.md instead — loop.sh points each iteration at that file for on-demand reading, which it cannot do for a field inside spec.json (spec.json also holds the issues array, which implementers must never open). This field remains valid for a short paragraph, or for a spec written before context.md existed. /to-issues reads whichever exists.

invariants.description: Rules that hold for every issue in this effort, phrased as absolutes an implementer can violate ('Sleeper player_id is the canonical player PK', 'no DB migrations'). INJECTED INTO EVERY ITERATION. Aim for 3-6.

out_of_scope.description: Adjacent work this effort deliberately does not do. INJECTED INTO EVERY ITERATION — this is the main defence against scope bleed.

verification.description: Shell commands that must pass before an issue counts as done ('npm test', 'npm run build'). INJECTED INTO EVERY ITERATION, and EXECUTED BY loop.sh in the repo root after the agent promises DONE — an issue is only recorded as done if they all exit 0. A command that cannot succeed here blocks the whole effort, so these must be real and runnable.

open_questions.description: Unresolved decisions. Not injected. /to-issues should resolve or explicitly defer these before writing issues.

issues.description: Ordered by priority: the loop picks the FIRST issue whose blockers are all done. Absent until /to-issues runs; loop.sh fails loudly if it is missing or empty.

ledger.description: Append-only record of completed issues, written by loop.sh from each iteration's DONE promise once the spec's verification commands have passed. INJECTED INTO EVERY ITERATION so a later issue learns what an earlier one built without reading its ticket.

issue.$comment: status and attempts are owned by loop.sh. /to-issues writes status once ('ready') and never writes attempts.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identity, unique within the spec. Used in blocked_by, in the ledger, and in the agent's DONE promise.

title.description: One line, imperative. Shown on the board and in the prompt.

status.description: Owned by loop.sh, never by the implementing agent. 'claimed' means an iteration started it and did not report done — it is re-picked on the next pass. Blocked is derived from blocked_by, not stored.

blocked_by.description: Ids of issues that must be done first. Empty array means immediately workable.

body.description: Path to the prose body, relative to the spec directory: issues/<id>.md. Null when the criteria say everything and no rationale is needed.

files.description: Paths or directories the implementer should start from, to skip a discovery phase.

model.description: Model this issue runs on, overriding loop.sh's default (--model, else CLAUDE_MODEL, else whatever claude is configured with). One of "haiku", "sonnet", "opus", or "fable"; omit or leave empty to take the default. Set it per issue when a ticket is mechanical enough for haiku or subtle enough to need opus.

criteria.description: Observable conditions that define done. The single source of truth — never duplicated into the body file. Injected verbatim as the ticket's definition of done, and judged against the iteration's git diff by loop.sh's clean-context criteria review — so each one must be evidenced by the diff, not by stated intent.

attempts.description: Append-only record of iterations that started this issue and did not complete it, written by loop.sh. Never authored by hand — /to-issues must not emit this field. The most recent entries are INJECTED INTO THE PROMPT on the next attempt so a fresh context window does not repeat a known-failing approach. Length is also the circuit breaker: at ISSUE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT the loop stops rather than burning more iterations.

reason.description: Short category of the failure: 'verification failed', 'no completion promise', 'reported blocked'.

detail.description: One line of specifics — the failing command, or what the agent said stopped it. Truncated by loop.sh before it is stored; may end with a pointer to the full log at <spec-dir>/attempts/<issue-id>-<n>.log.

outcome.description: One line: what now exists that did not before, named concretely enough for a later issue to use it.

commit.description: HEAD after the iteration that completed this issue, when the loop ran inside a git repo. Absent outside one, or when the iteration committed nothing.
